sights.w: A Middle Jōmon village above the Pacific — more than 100 pit-dwelling hollows, some 2 m deep, part of the 2021 UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites in Northern Japan.

A settlement where living and burial grounds were separated for millennia, with a 190 m U-shaped earthen mound; the Hakodate Jōmon Culture Center (with Hokkaido's only National Treasure, a hollow clay dogū) is beside it. UNESCO.

sights.address: Washinoki-chō, Mori, Kayabe District, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: Hokkaido's largest stone circle (Late Jōmon), a double ring of stones on a hill above Uchiura Bay — an associated site of the Jōmon World Heritage nomination.

sights.n: Kitakogane Shell Mound — Jōmon (北黄金貝塚)
sights.w: A Jōmon settlement with large shell middens facing Uchiura Bay and a 'water site' where tools were ritually sent back — UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites.

sights.n: Irie & Takasago Shell Mounds — Jōmon (入江・高砂貝塚)
sights.address: Takasago-chō, Tōyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: Two Jōmon sites a few hundred metres apart above Uchiura Bay — the Irie village shell mound and the Takasago burial ground. UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites.

sights.n: Kiusu Earthwork Burial Circles — Jōmon (キウス周堤墓群)
sights.w: Ring-shaped earthen burial enclosures up to 75 m across in a Chitose forest — among the largest Jōmon communal cemeteries. UNESCO Jōmon Prehistoric Sites.

sights.address: Sōbetsu Onsen, Sōbetsu, Usu District, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: One of the world's youngest mountains: a lava dome that rose out of a wheat field in 1943–45 to 398 m and still steams — beside the Usuzan Ropeway base.
A near-perfectly round caldera lake above Noboribetsu Onsen with no inflowing river — rated among Japan's clearest.

sights.n: Niseko Annupuri (ニセコアンヌプリ)
sights.address: Niseko / Kutchan, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: The 1,308 m volcano whose flanks carry the Niseko United ski areas (Grand Hirafu, Hanazono, Niseko Village, Annupuri) — famed for deep, dry powder and backcountry gates.

sights.address: Maeda, Kyōwa, Iwanai District, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: The loveliest of the Niseko range's marsh ponds — a 20-minute boardwalk through alpine bog to still water ringed by Todo firs.

sights.n: Fukidashi Park, Kyōgoku (ふきだし公園)
sights.w: Mount Yōtei's snowmelt gushes out here after decades underground — one of Japan's biggest spring discharges; locals fill bottles at the source.
